data.exact_reserve_text: During 2016, net ultimate claims in respect of prior underwriting years (2014 & prior) reduced by GBP 6.7m. This was mainly due to favourable claims development over the year in the Director's & Officers, Marine Liability and Aerospace classes. The Airline Liability class also benefited from a GBP 2.7m takedown in the large 2008 Air France loss. These reductions were offset by net ultimate claims increases in the A&H and General Liability classes, partly due to increased exposure estimates as inwards premium from binders were revised upwards.

data.standardized_narrative: At 31 December 2016 the syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding were GBP 411.418m. Analysis of the claims development triangle shows an overall favourable prior-year development on gross claims of approximately GBP 11.95m (c.2.9% of opening reserves) for underwriting years 2014 and prior, driven by favourable development in Directors & Officers, Marine Liability and Aerospace, partially offset by adverse development in Accident & Health and General Liability related to increased exposure estimates. The report states a net prior-year reduction of GBP 6.7m after reinsurance. Specific legacy large losses (notably a takedown on the 2008 Air France loss) and other technical energy losses are referenced as drivers of volatility.

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from the provision reconciliation (explicit). Prior year development gross amount was not stated directly in a single 'movement in prior years' gross line; gross PYD was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (pages 38-39). The report explicitly states a net prior-year reduction of GBP 6.7m (after reinsurance); the gross triangle-derived movement is approx -GBP 11.95m (release). Amounts for individual LOB movements are not quantified in gross terms in the narrative and therefore set to null. Event years for some named large losses (Samarco, Chevron Bigfoot, PMV) are not specified in the report and are therefore null.
